exact_target: I can construct evidence for a function family using patterns in graphs, equations, tables, and contexts.
I can apply family features to sort representations into linear, quadratic, exponential, absolute value, and other familiar forms.
I can determine which representation gives the strongest evidence for a function family when features seem similar.
Solve systems graphically and by elimination while interpreting the meaning of different solution types.
Analyze and compare linear relationships using multiple representations.
I can build translated graphs by moving key points and key features from a parent function.
I can use horizontal and vertical shifts to write equations for translated functions.
I can predict how changing values in an equation moves a graph left, right, up, or down.
Graph and interpret linear inequalities.
Graph linear functions and interpret key features.
I can design transformed graphs using stretches, compressions, reflections, and translations of parent functions.
I can apply transformation rules to key points and features across function families.
I can assess whether an equation, graph, or table represents the same transformed function.
Analyze and interpret systems of linear inequalities.
Interpret slope as a measure of constant rate of change.
I can formulate polynomial sums, differences, and products from area, perimeter, and expression contexts.
I can use structure and like terms to add, subtract, and multiply polynomial expressions.
I can extend polynomial operations to equivalent expressions written in different forms.
Solve systems using substitution and choose efficient forms for solving.
Write linear equations from graphs, tables, and situations.
I can construct connections between polynomial structure, quadratic graphs, and key features.
I can predict graph features from equivalent quadratic expressions.
I can critique whether a polynomial expression supports a claimed vertex, intercept, axis of symmetry, or direction of opening.
Create and solve systems that model real-world situations.
Use linear models to represent and interpret real-world data.
Interpret slope as constant rate of change across tables, graphs, and contexts and judge whether a rate is reasonable.
Graph linear functions and write linear equations from slope, intercepts, tables, graphs, and situations.
Compare linear relationships shown in different representations using slope, intercepts, and contextual meaning.
Build and use linear models for real-world data, make predictions, and judge model fit for the question being asked.
Accurately perform operations with integers, fractions, and decimals while interpreting results in mathematical and contextual situations.
source: Original Unit 1 Assessment Plan via current Framework
